correctness.rationale: A nonzero coefficient on each permutation cycle satisfies x^(2^L-1)=A^(-1). The obstruction A is uniform because the last weight appears to the first power. Each cycle contributes 1 or 1+d solutions independently. The total count is a PRODUCT; the reviewed proof correctly applies the permutation cycle index to complex moments of that product (not to t raised to the product), and independently gives an exact finite cycle-type/binomial probability formula. For F4 the logarithm base two becomes additive across cycles, yielding its valid probability-generating function, exact zero-idempotent law, and fourth-order variance. The standalone exhaustive program reproduced all 21 parameter cases and explicitly checked the F4 second-moment formula.

value.rationale: This gives a natural complete idempotent-count distribution in every dimension and every finite field for a graph-restricted perfect evolution-algebra ensemble, rather than a routine isolated small count. The F4 law has a parity obstruction, an explicit probability of no nonzero idempotent with sharp power-law decay, and quartic variance growth, giving a reusable benchmark and a genuine field-sensitive contrast with other random matrix ensembles.
